key_insight: Granger causality-informed DMD uses directional predictive dependencies to identify sparse flow models with improved prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: More reliable reduced-order models could support efficient prediction and analysis of complex unsteady flows.
method: Estimate conditional Granger causality from flow data.
Regularize DMD operator identification to suppress weakly supported interactions.
Preserve dynamically relevant couplings for prediction and modal analysis.
evidence_signal: Tests on a known linear system, lid-driven cavity flows, and a transonic turbulent jet showed improvements over standard DMD in operator identification, spectral robustness, or prediction accuracy.
watch_item: Granger causality measures predictive dependence, not necessarily physical causation; inferred couplings may depend on data quality and model choices.
paper_title: Causality-informed dynamic mode decomposition for unsteady flow analysis
